answer: To deter Sybil attacks and treat costless replication as a fable, an agent network can anchor identities to droplet telemetry. Nodes authenticate by placing a micro-droplet on a hydrophobic lotus texture and digitizing contact-angle decay under a calibrated zephyr. An attacker must run dedicated microfluidic rigs per identity, imposing real hardware and fluid replenishment costs. However, ambient humidity drifts alter evaporation rates, intermittently triggering false rejections.
